propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon, because _resolve_target treats any colon-bearing string as already-qualified; canonical Bedrock ids like 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' trigger this bug while unversioned aliases work by accident

The qualified/unqualified decision was made independently in two code paths (_resolve_target and infer_provider) using identical flawed logic, causing them to drift; consolidation into a single split_provider_qualifier function prevents future divergence

An explicitly configured provider must be checked before scanning the model string for punctuation, so no model id syntax can overrule or discard an explicit instruction; without this guard order, _resolve_target('openai:gpt-4o', provider='bedrock') still silently drops the configured provider
Conflicting inline qualifiers and explicitly configured providers must raise rather than silently picking a winner, since either choice discards an operator's explicit instruction

Error messages currently report fragments of model ids as though they were provider names, e.g. blaming 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1' when the operator configured 'bedrock' and the actual issue is the colon in their model id
